weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start to seg3:end shows a generic rocket launching from a beach beside a gantry. The near-versus-far claim exists only as the text '250 miles' and a 17-digit '29,400,000,000,000,000' overlaid on the rocket. Nothing shows the Cold Atom Lab in orbit or the nebula's distance.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The scene draws a launch, which is an event, not the distance relationship. The narration's claim ('extreme cold brought close') has no physical form, so a raw digit string carries it.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show the distance itself. The ISS with the Cold Atom Lab glowing sits just overhead in a frame Data can reach (he hauls it into view or lifts a scope to it). The camera then pulls back across the sky toward the far-off Boomerang Nebula until it is a speck, or a ruler of 250-mile ticks runs out past the edge of the frame. Show one headline number and say 'quadrillions' in words, not 17 digits.
